# SideSchedule

> SideSchedule is a day-calendar sidebar for macOS 13 or later. It reserves a strip at the left or right screen edge the way the Dock does, so other windows can't cover it. Free for 14 days, then €12.99 once (two Macs per licence). Made by didact in Austria. Launch offer: 50% off for the first 100 buyers.

## What it does

- Shows today's events from Apple Calendar, which covers iCloud, Google, Exchange and CalDAV accounts. It reads, creates, renames, moves and deletes real events through EventKit.
- Keeps its space: windows that slide under the sidebar get pushed back out. This needs the macOS Accessibility permission; the app only moves window frames and never reads window content.
- Meeting notes typed in the sidebar save as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter in a folder you choose, ready for Obsidian or Logseq. Recurring meetings get one note per occurrence.
- Joins Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex and FaceTime calls in one click, opening the native app when it's installed.
- Shows the next free 30 minutes in the header. Drag events to reschedule, drop a file or text selection to block time. All-day events and Reminders have their own section.
- Auto-hide shrinks it to a thin strip that still shows the join button and a countdown.
- Works on any display, left or right edge, and follows to another screen when a monitor is unplugged.
- Interface in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese.
- Quick Add: a global shortcut (default Ctrl+Option+N) opens a text field. Type or dictate a sentence such as "Call with Bob tomorrow at half past three pm", check the preview, press Return. Understands dates, times, durations, all-day events and spoken forms in all six app languages; dictation uses macOS dictation (microphone button).
- Optional reminders before events (off by default): system notification, in-sidebar banner or both, several lead times, snooze, filters (only events with a meeting link, skip declined events, calendar selection).
- Optional Focus around meetings (off by default): runs a shortcut from the Shortcuts app when a meeting starts and when it ends, for example one that switches a Focus on.
- New onboarding that explains the permission prompts before macOS asks.
- Local-first: no account, no analytics, no telemetry. Network calls are licence checks (Lemon Squeezy) and update checks (GitHub).

## Limits

- Native fullscreen apps: the sidebar draws over them instead of shrinking them. This is on the roadmap.
- Not on the Mac App Store. Distributed as a signed, notarized DMG.
